In soft clay, peat, flowing sand, with a very high groundwater table

If the trench is short and shallow
Here the shear strength of the soil is low, and the water pressure or the risk of slurry loss is high. Hard clay and rock make excavation difficult (a hydrofraise is needed there), not stability.
When is a hydrofraise (trench cutter) justified rather than a grab?
In rock, very hard clay, at great depth and with accuracy requirements
For a short, shallow wall in loose sand
If the cheapest solution is needed
The cutter works accurately in any soil and rock, to great depth – but it is very expensive. In Hungary it was used for metro line 4 (Fővám tér: 48.3 m).
